proof_audit.topic: Sharp continuity target and observational nonidentification
proof_audit.reasoning: Consistency identifies the observed conditional versions separately on each open side. Positive support plus continuity makes the potential-outcome versions unique at the cutoff; taking limits yields their difference. Giving both potential outcomes the observed discontinuous curve reproduces the same observed law with zero effect.
proof_audit.boundary: The estimand uses continuous limits, not an arbitrary conditional value on the zero-probability cutoff. Continuity does not identify every score or randomize a finite window.

proof_audit.topic: Boundary weighted least squares and Gaussian law
proof_audit.reasoning: The two weighted normal equations have determinant S0 S2−S1²>0 when distinct positively weighted scores exist. Their inverse gives each outcome weight. Summing weights and score-weighted weights proves constant/linear reproduction. Independent fixed-score Gaussian errors yield the exact linear normal law with variance equal to the sum of squared weights times variances.
proof_audit.boundary: Positive kernels may generate negative equivalent outcome weights. The variance/normality conclusion is conditional on fixed scores and known independent Gaussian errors, not a generic RD theorem.

proof_audit.reasoning: Quadratic reproduction gives v=(3,−3,1). The finite difference qhat=50(Y1−2Y2+Y3) and adding the estimated curvature difference/30 changes w into v. The independent two-side covariance is 2σ² w·[(5/3)(1,−2,1)]=0; correction variance is 100σ²/3 and total is 38σ². A separate Taylor remainder bound uses absolute rather than signed squared-score weights. The triangle inequality on the central Gaussian event proves at least 95% coverage with deterministic bias bound plus z SE.
proof_audit.boundary: Zero covariance is design-specific. The conservative B=13/25 need not be sharp. No generic unknown-variance or adaptive-bandwidth coverage follows.

proof_audit.topic: Fixed-grid identities, optimal leading width and rate undersmoothing
proof_audit.reasoning: Insert finite sums of j, j² and j³ into the intercept formula. The resulting affine weights give exact constant/linear reproduction, quadratic moment and squared-weight identities. Exact quadratic bias and variance yield the leading MSE; differentiating for nonzero curvature difference gives h_opt^5=72σ²/(delta_q² n). Since n h_opt diverges, integer rounding is asymptotically negligible. Substitution gives absolute standardized bias 1/2 and the stated normal coverage. Multiplying h by fixed r multiplies standardized bias by r^(5/2); h=n^(−a), 1/5<a<1, removes it while retaining diverging local sample size.
proof_audit.boundary: n counts available observations on EACH side; total available rows are 2n. The optimum is for a leading expansion with known curvature and is not used at delta_q=0. A fixed fraction is not rate undersmoothing.

proof_audit.reasoning: Taylor remainder and reproduction bound absolute bias by (Lplus+Lminus) h² sum|w|/2. Cauchy–Schwarz and the exact squared-weight sum give sum|w|<=sqrt(10); exact variance is <=20σ²/k. Squared bias plus variance tends to zero when h tends to zero and k diverges. The deterministic bound also permits the finite known-Gaussian interval argument.
proof_audit.boundary: This proof does not establish the causal continuity restriction, a score-density law, unknown-variance coverage or validity after outcome-driven bandwidth search.

proof_audit.reasoning: Constant type probabilities and continuous within-type potential means give common one-sided composite limits. Exclusion and no interference permit conditioning on receipt type. Under monotonicity nonswitchers cancel; the receipt jump is pC and the outcome jump is pC times the complier mean effect. Positive pC permits division. Direct eligibility and fully specified defier variants alter different premises.
proof_audit.boundary: The resulting effect is local to compliers in the common cutoff population, distinct from the assignment ITT and cutoff ATE. No weak-first-stage normal inference is supplied.

proof_audit.topic: Simplex existence, fit uniqueness and weight selection
proof_audit.reasoning: A continuous loss on the nonempty compact simplex attains its minimum. Positive-definite V makes the midpoint of two distinct optimal fitted predictors strictly improve the loss, so the fit is unique. Different optimal weights exist exactly when a nonzero feasible zero-sum direction has zero donor-predictor image. Augmented full column rank is a stronger sufficient condition. Sequential coordinate minimization on compact optimal sets defines the lexicographically smallest optimizer.
proof_audit.boundary: An algorithmic tie rule does not establish causal identification. Zero donor weights are allowed. Numerical enumeration covers the stated small identity-V cases and certifies the global optimum by KKT.

proof_audit.topic: Noiseless factor rank, future row span and approximate-fit bound
proof_audit.reasoning: For untreated training outcome vectors, e=Fpre(lambda1−Lambda0 w). Under full column rank, L=(Fpre prime Fpre)^−1 Fpre prime is a left inverse, giving loading error Le. Exact fit yields zero future error; approximate fit gives |f prime L e|<=||f prime L|| ||e||. Alternatively a future factor row in the row span has f prime=a prime Fpre, so exact fit suffices at that date even if Fpre is rank deficient.
proof_audit.boundary: No anticipation in training, unaffected donors, the maintained common-factor structure and the relevant rank/row-space condition are explicit. A new factor absent from every preperiod or added fit noise breaks this proof.

proof_audit.topic: Support loss, hidden factors and contamination
proof_audit.reasoning: Deleting donor C reduces the feasible training set to a segment, whose strictly convex scalar loss gives weights 3/10 and 7/10. The exact left-inverse discrepancies explain changed gaps. A treated-only post factor with zero prehistory preserves the complete observed panel while changing untreated post values and effects. Separately, a donor-B spillover changes observed donor values and weighted predictions.
proof_audit.boundary: The hidden-factor example is observational equivalence; the spillover example is a changed-data intervention. Holdouts with the factor identically zero cannot identify its future loading.

proof_audit.topic: Optimal-weight range versus sharp causal interval
proof_audit.reasoning: Identical prefit columns make every two-donor convex weight optimal. Post forecasts are the affine map 8−6w and gaps −1+6w, so their closed ranges are attained. Under the additional fixed-mixture restriction, every w supplies an admissible untreated post outcome and treatment effect reproducing observations, proving sharpness. Without it a treated-only post factor produces counterfactuals outside the donor range.
proof_audit.boundary: A range over optimal forecasts alone is not an identified causal set. Lexicographic selection produces one reproducible forecast but cannot narrow the causal set without added information.

proof_audit.reasoning: Under the sharp null the panel is fixed for every label. Replay the full prescribed fitting/statistic algorithm for each label. Inclusive upper-tail probabilities are constant across ties and monotone in scores. Any nonempty rejection set is an entire upper tail with mass equal to the p-value at its lowest score, no greater than alpha. The declared infinity and zero categories fit the same ordering argument.
proof_audit.boundary: The theorem needs the actual known assignment probabilities and a sharp null for all units/dates; it is not a weak average-effect test or automatic observational calibration. Filtering and donor selection must be specified and replayed.

exercise_solution_audit.exact_prompt: Prove sharp RD identification using continuous conditional versions and positive score support around zero. Explain why a value assigned arbitrarily on R=0 is not the estimand. Construct example 1's zero-effect observational alternative and identify the assumption it violates.
exercise_solution_audit.independent_solution: Taking each observed one-sided limit gives m1(0)−m0(0). Positive support prevents two continuous versions from differing at zero. P(R=0)=0 leaves arbitrary noncontinuous event values irrelevant. Setting both potentials to the observed piecewise curve supplies zero effects with the identical (R,D,Y) law and fails continuity.
exercise_solution_audit.prompt_match_and_limits: Both the uniqueness argument and full observational counterexample answer the exact prompt; no finite-window randomization claimed.
exercise_solution_audit.status: Complete prompt and corresponding solution read; mathematical reasoning and stated numerical results checked.

exercise_solution_audit.exact_prompt: Derive example 1's finite-window mean contrast and evaluate h=1 and h=1/5. Prove that the separate U,V sorting construction has a continuous uniform score density, an observed jump 1 and zero causal effect. What does this say about a passing density diagnostic?
exercise_solution_audit.independent_solution: Uniform-window first/second moments give right 5+h+h²/3 and left 2−h/2+h²/3; differences 9/2 and 33/10. Fair independent sign times |V| yields density 1/2 on each side, while U and hence the observed outcome jump from 0 to 1. Both potentials equal U, so effects are identically zero.
exercise_solution_audit.prompt_match_and_limits: A passing density diagnostic cannot prove the missing potential-outcome restriction; the complete score/type law is supplied.
exercise_solution_audit.status: Complete prompt and corresponding solution read; mathematical reasoning and stated numerical results checked.

exercise_solution_audit.exact_prompt: Derive the same-data quadratic bias correction, including the variance of the correction and its covariance with the original estimate. Compute the coverage from using the old variance afterward. Separately derive the bounded-curvature bias bound and the known-Gaussian 95% radius in example 2.
exercise_solution_audit.topic: Estimated correction versus deterministic bias bound
exercise_solution_audit.independent_solution: The correction vector is (5/3)(1,−2,1); its two-side variance is 100σ²/3 and covariance with the original jump is exactly zero. The total is 38σ². Old-variance coverage is 0.5078205300463543. Absolute squared-score moment 13/150 gives B=13/25 and radius 0.943400612067412.
exercise_solution_audit.prompt_match_and_limits: The same-data covariance is explicitly computed. The Taylor-bound interval is a separate conservative result with known noise and fixed curvature bounds.

exercise_solution_audit.exact_prompt: Prove all four fixed-grid weight identities in section 3 and derive exact quadratic bias and variance. Derive the leading MSE-optimal bandwidth, its limiting standardized bias and conventional coverage. Explain why a fixed half-width fraction is not rate undersmoothing, give a valid power rate, and prove bounded-curvature mean-square consistency.
exercise_solution_audit.independent_solution: Direct sums establish all four grid identities. Bias is −delta_q(k+1)(k+2)/(6n²), variance 4σ²(2k+1)/(k(k−1)). Leading h_opt^5=72σ²/(delta_q² n) gives standardized bias magnitude 1/2 and coverage 0.9209024658394034. Fixed fraction r leaves r^(5/2)/2. Power 1/4 gives diverging local k and vanishing scaled bias. Uniform sqrt(10) weight and 20σ²/k variance bounds prove MSE consistency.
exercise_solution_audit.prompt_match_and_limits: The analytic proof uses arbitrary integer k; focused exact checks at k=2,3,7,20 test its arithmetic. n is per side; fixed fractions and power rates are distinguished.
exercise_solution_audit.status: Complete prompt and corresponding solution read; mathematical reasoning and stated numerical results checked.

exercise_solution_audit.topic: All placebo refits and actual tails
exercise_solution_audit.independent_solution: All four fits project to (1,1), have pre-MSE 1 and give gaps 7/2,−3,−2,3/2. Uniform inclusive tails are 1/4,1/2,3/4,1; actual-law tails are 7/10,4/5,9/10,1. Rejection at 1/4 has probability 1/4 under uniform design, 7/10 for false uniform ranking under the alternative design, and zero with correct alternative weights. No 5% rejection is possible in the uniform four-label experiment.

exercise_solution_audit.exact_prompt: A report divides an MSE-optimal RD bandwidth by two, treats a nonsignificant density test as proof of random assignment, and applies the original standard error after bias correction. Its synthetic-control section chooses donors after viewing post outcomes, equates perfect prefit with causal identification, and calls a uniform placebo rank an exact p-value for an observational intervention. Give six distinct objections, two feasible repairs with explicit assumptions and limitations, and a defensible conclusion. The solution rubric allocates 12 points.
exercise_solution_audit.independent_solution: Six distinct objections address fixed-fraction smoothing, density nonrejection, old post-correction variance, post-outcome donor choice, identification from prefit and false observational randomization language. Two repairs require explicit RD and SC inference/identification assumptions and acknowledge remaining limits. A defensible conclusion separates description, causal identification and calibrated uncertainty.
exercise_solution_audit.prompt_match_and_limits: Rubric sums to 12: six objections at 1 each, two repairs at 2 each and conclusion at 2. It does not require a chosen sign, brand or unsupported empirical assertion.

teaching_review.progression: Cutoff target and observational counterexamples precede estimation. Exact known-Gaussian calculations lead to bandwidth rates, then fuzzy identification. Synthetic fitting precedes rank conditions, support failures and placebo probability laws. Every exercise uses a taught calculation or proved argument.
teaching_review.law_separation: Continuous-score populations, fixed-score Gaussian sequences, cutoff-type mixtures, noiseless factor tables and finite randomized labels are explicitly separate laws.
teaching_review.teach_back: Answered: smooth density and exact prefit are diagnostics, not proof of unobserved counterfactual restrictions. Factor/support conditions support a causal forecast; a sharp null and actual assignment law support finite rank calibration.
teaching_review.retention: Answered and recomputed: k=2 weights (2,−1), jump variance 10σ²; n^(−1/4) has proper rate under the declared Gaussian sequence; drop-C discrepancy at s=3 is 6/5; candidate A proper alternative-law tail is 7/10.

checker_contract.API: Quiet read-only check() returns strict-JSON-compatible summary; default CLI calls check() silently. Helper domains are intentionally bounded original cases, not an arbitrary estimator or user-data engine.
checker_contract.independent_methods: Exact Fraction antiderivatives, normal equations, active-face simplex optimization with KKT, separate augmented affine system, factor left inverse and finite actual-law tail sums. No root blueprint/checker or external library imported.
checker_contract.bounded_domain: Exact int/Fraction inputs and inverted matrix entries have magnitude <=10^6; degree 1 or 2, with 2..32 strictly one-sided score rows and supported weighted polynomial rank; grid 2<=k<=32 and k<=n<=100000; 2..4 fully specified positive-mass compliance types; 2..3 donor/predictor coordinates; 2..8 supported assignment labels. Nonfinite, boolean, negative kernel/error and missing-rank/probability cases reject explicitly. These helpers serve the bounded original cases, not an unrestricted estimation API.

limitations: Author checks and finite examples do not verify empirical continuity, exclusion, factor support, interference absence or an observational assignment law.
Known-Gaussian fixed-score inference is restricted; no general RBC, unknown-variance adaptive bandwidth, weak-first-stage or stochastic synthetic-control theorem is claimed.
Runtime helpers cover the declared small finite laws; no generic statistical software, donor-search optimization or large-data algorithm is supplied.
Working files remain subject to separate review and dependency-ordered canonical promotion by root. No shared catalogue, accepted status or publishing action is part of this author scope.
